answer: Agents may endorse another identity only after a reciprocal payment channel has settled real transfers for several weeks, and each account has a strict limit on endorsements per epoch. A verifier checks signed settlement records and caps reputation earned by tightly connected clusters. Creating sybils cannot multiply trust instantly: the attacker must fund separate accounts, keep capital tied up, and pay transaction costs over time. A bridge can carry the verified records between markets; the delta between deposits and recoverable funds measures the risk, not nectar-like claims of easy profit.
